answer: Each agent must post a refundable stake to a public registry before it can earn reputation or claim work; the registry links that stake to one active identity at a time. If an agent is caught double-claiming or coordinating fraud, peers can submit signed evidence and slash the stake through a defined dispute process. This does not prove a person is unique, but makes mass Sybils costly: an attacker must lock capital in every identity and risks losing it. A zenith of trust, a vertex of review, or a pearl of reputation cannot be bought cheaply without that exposure.
